name: Sheet Metal Bend Allowance
blurb: flat length from K-factor and bend radius
intro: The flat (blank) length of a part with one bend, from two flange lengths, the sheet thickness, the inside radius and the K-factor, the fraction of the thickness where the neutral axis sits. Standard bend allowance and bend deduction formulas are used. The K-factor can be typed in, estimated with DIN 6935, or taken from a common rule-of-thumb table.

inputs.label: Inside bend radius R
inputs.help: Air bending: about the V-die opening / 6 to / 8, but never less than the punch radius.

inputs.label: The angle is the
options: Bend angle (turned through: 90 for an L)

inputs.label: K-factor
inputs.help: 0 = neutral axis on the inside face, 0.5 = mid-thickness. Usually 0.3 to 0.5.

examples.title: 2 mm steel L-bracket, 50 x 30 outside, R2

usage: Give thickness, inside radius and flange lengths in mm and the angle in degrees (say whether it is the bend angle or the included angle, and whether flanges are to the outside or inside mould line). Choose kmode din, table or manual (then give k). It returns the K-factor used, bend allowance, outside setback, bend deduction and the flat length, plus a table of flat length against K-factor. Use it to size a blank or check a CAD flat pattern.
sources: Bend allowance BA = θ(R + K·T), setback OSSB = tan(θ/2)(R + T), bend deduction BD = 2·OSSB − BA: Machinery's Handbook, sheet metal section
DIN 6935:2011 correction factor k = 0.65 + 0.5·lg(R/T) for R/T < 5 (K = k/2)
K-factor table by hardness: common press-brake rule of thumb
